summary: Initial POC scoping for Stratus Analytics focused on selecting open models for a multilingual document understanding workflow. Covered success criteria (latency, throughput, quality thresholds), workload sizing, shortlist of open models with tradeoffs, benchmark plan, and timelines for a 1-week benchmark and 6-week POC.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-09-30 16:00 PDT | Duration: 58m
Attendees: Maya Chen, Liam O'Connor, Sofia Alvarez (Redwood) - Priya Nair, Carlos Mendes, Anna Lee, Tom Hsu (Stratus Analytics)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. This is Maya from Redwood Inference, AE on the deal, with Liam our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Priya: Good, thanks. Busy week but ready.
[00:10] Liam: Hi all, quick intro from me — I'm Liam, will mostly be on the technical scoping.
[00:15] Priya: Great. Our goal today is to scope a POC for document classification + multi-lingual extraction across English, Spanish, and Portuguese.
[00:25] Maya: Perfect. We'll go through success criteria, expected workload, candidate open models, and propose a 1-week benchmark then a 6-week POC if things look good.
[00:33] 
[01:05] Tom: Quick context: we run nightly batch ingestion of ~120k docs/day, peak concurrent interactive queries around 80 QPS during business hours, and spikes to ~150 QPS for dashboards. Latency target for interactive is 300-500ms end to end, 95th percentile. Cost is a big factor — we need predictable unit costs.
[01:25] Liam: Okay that's helpful. For the POC we typically size by concurrent tokens and average tokens per request. Do you have an average tokens per doc or per query?
[01:35] Anna: Our typical user query hits about 150-400 tokens; the extraction prompts can be longer (up to 900 tokens) for multi-field extraction.
[01:45] Maya: So for initial benchmark let's target 100 QPS synthetic with a mix: 70% short queries (200 tokens), 30% long extraction (800 tokens). That aligns with your peak but gives headroom.
[01:55] Priya: Works for us. Success criteria — we want F1 >= 0.87 on key entity extraction, 95th pctl latency <= 600ms in hosted mode for short queries, and cost per 1k tokens below our threshold (we'll share the exact number).
[02:10] 
[03:00] Liam: On model selection: since you prefer open models, we've shortlisted a few that balance quality and latency. Quick list: Llama 2 70B (quantized), Mistral-Instruct (mix), Falcon 40B-Instruct (quantized), and Llama-3-34B variants; plus small specialist models for multilingual tuning (e.g., XLM-R finetuned adapters).
[03:20] Priya: Any concerns around hallucination and extraction accuracy? We care a lot about precision.
[03:28] Liam: Right. In our experience, larger models like Llama 3 34B (or 70B) give better extraction F1 out of the box, but quantized 70B kernels can increase latency or variability unless you use the Dedicated runtime with optimized kernels. Mistral-style models are often lighter and lower cost but need more prompt engineering. Falcon 40B is a middle ground.
[03:50] Carlos: We likely need to run the models in a private VPC for data residency and egress controls. Can Redwood support private deployment and also host a short benchmark?
[03:58] Maya: Yes — we offer both hosted API for quick benchmarking and Redwood Private (VPC) for production. For the 1-week benchmark we can run hosted with data obfuscation or a dedicated private environment depending on your compliance needs.
[04:12] Priya: We'll prefer private if possible, but for speed we can start hosted with obfuscated samples. Security docs are important.
[04:18] Sofia: We'll share the SOC2, ISO, KMS integration notes, and a private deployment checklist right after.
[04:25] 
[05:00] Tom: On throughput, do you have recommendations for batching and KV cache? We have many repeated prefixes in prompts.
[05:08] Liam: Yes, Redwood runtime supports prefix/KV caching — we can get a lot of benefit on chat-style or multi-turn extraction. For your workload, enabling KV caching for repeated document contexts should reduce effective token compute by ~15-30% depending on cache hit rates. Batching can improve throughput but increases tail latency; with your latency SLO we recommend conservative batching with latency-aware routing.
[05:30] Priya: Good to know. What about quantization? We want to reduce cost but not lose extraction accuracy.
[05:36] Liam: For Llama 2/3 70B, 4-bit quantization (QLoRA-style or int4 inference) often keeps quality close for many tasks but extraction precision can degrade for some entity types. Our recommendation: run benchmarks with 34B int8 and 70B int4 quantized variants, compare F1 on your annotated set. That gives a clear tradeoff curve between cost and quality.
[05:58] 
[07:10] Anna: Multilingual — do any of these models have a clear advantage for Spanish/Portuguese?
[07:16] Liam: Mistral variants and large Llama family models are decent multi-lingual pros, but specialist finetuned adapters on XLM-R or a small finetune stage often gives the best lift for low-resource languages. For the POC we recommend evaluating base open model performance first, then a short adapter fine-tune on ~1-2k examples per language if needed.
[07:40] 
[09:00] Priya: Benchmarks — what will you need from us?
[09:05] Maya: We'll need a sample corpus (~2k docs that reflect production distribution), a labeled validation set for F1 (200-500 labeled examples per extraction field), and a target prompts file. We'll provide a benchmark template with metrics, scripts, and a cost estimator.
[09:22] Priya: We have an internal labeling team; can deliver labels within a week.
[09:27] Maya: Great. For metrics we'll capture F1/precision/recall per field, latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99), tokens per second, and cost per 1k tokens. We'll also capture failure cases for hallucinations.
[09:40] 
[11:00] Carlos: Network constraints: we have strict egress rules and will need to run in our VPC eventually. For the hosted benchmark, we'll whitelist Redwood IPs but prefer private if feasible.
[11:10] Liam: Noted. We'll prepare a private benchmark option. Also we'll provide a deployment checklist for firewall/NAT and KMS.
[11:18] 
[14:10] Maya: Timeline suggestion: share benchmark template + security pack by 2026-10-02, Stratus provides sample corpus and labels by 2026-10-01, Redwood runs 1-week benchmark 2026-10-05 to 2026-10-12, followed by a review and decision to start 6-week POC (tentative kickoff 2026-10-15). Does that align?
[14:28] Priya: That aligns with our internal timelines. We'll aim to have label deliverables by the 1st.
[14:33] 
[18:00] Tom: For the shortlist can you enumerate expected deployment modes and perf tradeoffs per model?
[18:07] Liam: Sure, quick summary:
- Llama 3 34B: Good quality, lower cost than 70B, strong extraction baseline; runs well quantized on Dedicated with int8; good multilingual baseline.
- Llama 3 70B (quantized): Best raw quality but higher cost; needs optimized kernels or Dedicated to keep latency SLOs.
- Mistral-Instruct (40-70B families): Strong latency and cost profile for generation; sometimes weaker on precision tasks without prompt engineering.
- Falcon 40B: Balanced; often faster in some kernels, reasonable F1 after prompt tuning.
- Specialist adapters / XLM-R + small LM: Best for targeted multilingual lift with minimal cost increase.

[20:10] Priya: Is there a recommended default for the benchmark if we can't test everything?
[20:16] Maya: Start with Llama 3 34B (int8) and Falcon 40B (quant) plus one Mistral variant. If those don't hit F1, escalate to 70B quantized for the quality run. That gives a cost/quality sweep quickly.
[20:30] 
[25:00] Anna: Any pitfalls from other customers doing similar POCs?
[25:06] Liam: Common pitfalls: 1) not using representative prompt distribution — lab sets that are too clean can overstate quality; 2) ignoring cache-hit patterns which can change cost estimates; 3) skipping adapter fine-tune for multilingual needs. We build the benchmark to surface those.
[25:25] Priya: Makes sense.
[30:00] Maya: Security/compliance recap: we'll share SOC2 docs, KMS integration notes, option for HSM if required, and details on audit logs/retention in Redwood Private.
[30:12] Carlos: Good. We'll review the security pack.
[34:00] Liam: For the hosted 1-week run we'll set up isolated model endpoints and provide per-route latency + cost dashboards so you can evaluate economics. If you go Private we'll provide the deployment runbook.
[34:30] Priya: For cost granularity, we want token-level cost breakdowns by route.
[34:36] Sofia: That's standard in Redwood Console — we'll share sample dashboards.
[40:00] Maya: Ok let's recap next steps — we'll send benchmark template, security docs, and a cost estimator. Stratus to provide sample corpus and labels. We'll schedule the 1-week benchmark window. After the benchmark we'll review and decide whether to continue to the 6-week POC with private deployment.
[40:20] Priya: Sounds good. One last question — are you able to support canary rollouts and automatic fallbacks to smaller models if load spikes?
[40:28] Liam: Yes, Redwood supports routing policies, canary deploys and automatic fallback to cheaper model variants or regional fallbacks to maintain availability. We'll include an example policy.
[40:40] Tom: Great.
[55:00] Maya: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with all artifacts and a calendar invite for the kickoff.
[55:08] Priya: Thanks, looking forward.

End of transcript.
